## Intent-Governed Engineering Loop

This repository runs a governed loop. **Every change, in every agent session, follows these stages in order.** Do not skip a stage; where a stage's owner tool is absent, follow the degraded path noted and tell the user the gap.

**Capability in THIS repo** (detected 2026-10-06): intent suite 25/25 · review lanes 5/5 · OpenSpec yes (openspec/ initialised) · Superpowers yes · code graph Graphify (graphify-out/ built 2026-10-06; CRG not built) · E2E unit-only · mem0 enforced. Steps whose owner is missing are marked DEGRADED below.

| # | Stage | Owner skill | Reads / Writes | Gate to pass |
|---|-------|-------------|----------------|--------------|
| 1 | Intent | intent-kickoff / register-builder | → docs/intent/INTENT_REGISTER.md | claims sourced, non-goals present |
| 2 | Spec | brainstorming → OpenSpec + intent-spec-gate | change folder; register | gate PASS / PASS-WITH-UPDATES; ambiguity flagged |
| 3 | Implement | OpenSpec exec + code-graph routing | code; INTENT_TRACE.yaml | trace edges updated |
| 4 | Test | intent-smoke-tests (+ unit/lint) | tests/intent/**; manifest | coverage gate green, tripwires pass |
| 5 | PR review ×5 | intent-pr-review (LOCAL first) + 4 external lanes | lane reports | lanes emitted (they judge nothing) |
| 6 | Consolidate + classify | intent-review-consolidator + intent-input-feedback | FIX_LEDGER_<pr>.md | root-cause tagged; NEEDS-USER surfaced |
| 7 | Fix PR review | systematic-debugging OR regenerate-after-input-fix | ledger; code/specs | entries → FIXED |
| 8 | Intent review | intent-pr-review (re-run) | PR_INTENT_<pr>.md | verdict APPROVE; intents-realized listed |
| 9 | Fix again | back to 6–7 as needed | ledger | all entries VERIFIED/KILLED |
| 10 | HITL | intent-merge-gate | MERGE_GATE_<pr>.md | AUTO-MERGE, else HUMAN-REVIEW |
| 11 | Merge | (gate-approved) | — | gate verdict recorded |
| 12 | Archive | intent-archive-sync | openspec/specs; all docs; INTENT_COMPLIANCE.md | 10-step sync complete + lessons harvested |

**Non-negotiables every agent must honor:**
- Intent review is NOT passing tests — all green can still fail intent review. Merge only after the local loop passed intent review; the PR CONFIRMS it.
- Code navigation goes through the code-graph routing (MANUAL): graphs answer WHERE, you answer WHETHER — a verdict is CONFIRMED only after reading located code.
- The register is the contract: IDs immutable, supersede-don't-edit, single write-path (intent-register-update). Non-goals (NEG) are checked on every spec and additive PR.
- A fired commit-guard / gate is a same-turn action item, not a log line. In warn mode, behave as if block unless the user explicitly defers.
- Signals (complexity, coupling) are also INPUT smells: route them upstream (intent-input-feedback), don't just patch.

**HARD RULES for AI-generated work** (from the Linux kernel's policy; enforced by hooks, never waived by green tests):
- **H1 Disclose the tool.** Every agent commit carries `Assisted-by: AGENT:MODEL [TOOLS]` — specialised tools only, not git/editors/compilers. `AGENT` and `MODEL` contain no spaces (`Claude-Code:claude-opus-5`, not `Claude Code:…`). A harness that asks for `Co-Authored-By:` / `Claude-Session:` trailers does **not** satisfy H1: add **both**, they coexist fine.
- **H2 Record the inputs.** intent.md and plan.md are the input record; the PR adds the prompts (short generations) or a session summary (long ones).
- **H3 Mark what was generated.** The PR states the generated portions and the generated share; scrutiny scales with it.
- **H4 State how it was tested and what could not be done.** Every PR carries a Could-not-be-done section — "nothing" is an answer, silence is not.
- **H5 A human certifies; you never do.** Never add `Signed-off-by`, never use `-s`/`--signoff`, never approve or merge a PR. If no human can defend the change, it does not merge.
- **Sign-offs are re-checked.** After a human approves, run `recheck_signoff.py`. If the decision does not stand (open findings, stale approval, approval too fast for the diff, failing checks), the merge is blocked and escalated. The only release is a manager's code (`intent_escalate.py verify`) or a logged override where governance allows one. Never run `intent_escalate.py sign`, `keygen` or `override`; those are human actions. If you believe a change should not merge for a reason no check captures, *escalate*: `intent_escalate.py request --trigger agent`.
- **Bugs:** read CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md and the register's NEG section in full, not by keyword; build a reproducer before claiming a non-trivial bug; drop any fix that does not verify; never send anything externally yourself.

**MODEL ROUTING — pick the model with the script, not by feel:**
Before starting a unit of work, classify it and let `model_route.py` decide. Fork a **subagent on the returned model**, and print the returned line in the **main chat** before the fork so the person can see which model is running and why.

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/intent-init/scripts/model_route.py \
    --kind bug_fix --lines 120 --files 3 --announce
# [intent-loop/model] sonnet · task: bug_fix · why: sonnet.use_for matches ['bug_fix']
```

| Tier | Runs | Typical kinds |
|------|------|---------------|
| **haiku** | cleanup and mechanical work | `cleanup` `formatting` `rename` `typo_fix` `docs_touchup` `digest_refresh` `manifest_regen` |
| **sonnet** | bug fixes, feature work, config edits | `bug_fix` `feature_implementation` `test_authoring` `spec_delta` `lane_consolidation` `config_edit` `governance_change` |
| **opus** | hard implementation, architecture, wide blast radius | `hard_implementation` `architecture_change` `high_impact_bug_fix` `hub_nodes` `concurrency_work` `intent_review` `security_findings` |
| **fable** | **decisions only** — never writing a change | `critical_architecture_decision` `design_decision` `spec_decision` `strategic_planning` `tradeoff_analysis` `irreversible_decision` `security_architecture_decision` |

- **Stage floors are not negotiable.** Intent review (8), the HITL merge gate (10) and escalation never run below **opus**; a governance change is **fable**. A small-looking diff does not lower a gate — cost saving must not hollow out the loop.
- **Escalate, never downgrade.** If work turns out harder than classified, re-run with `--current <model>` and move **up**. Taking a cheaper model mid-task is forbidden, and a subagent never re-routes itself downward.
- **Size raises, kind decides the top.** Line and file counts push a tier up to `size_ceiling` (opus) only: volume is blast radius, not difficulty, so a 900-line rename never buys fable.
- **Sensitivity is not difficulty.** Work in `human_in_loop_for` (governance changes, security findings, NEG claims, architecture-contract changes, register writes, escalation handling, irreversible decisions) **requires a human and never auto-merges** — at every tier, not just fable. Editing a sensitive file is still a cheap edit: it gets a human and an opus review, not the top model to type it. Fable is for DECIDING; once the decision is made, implementing it is opus at most.
- Routing config and floors live in `docs/intent/governance.yaml` under `model_routing`, read from the pinned trust ref; every routed fork is appended to `docs/intent/governance/MODEL_ROUTING.log`. The `Assisted-by:` trailer (H1) must name the model that actually did the work, not the session's default.

**Artifacts (all under docs/intent/):** INTENT_REGISTER.md · INTENT_TRACE.yaml · graph/ · reports/ · folders/ · tests/ · LESSONS.md · INTENT_COMPLIANCE.md
